name: DC-net cell end to end (tools/dcnet_cell_lab.py)

setup.books: padbook's make/accept flow: each contribution kernel XOR Nitrokey 3 output (no touch), sealed to the partner's ML-KEM-768 + X25519 key, opened, combined, stored opaquely; storage keys stand in for each member's own Nitrokey hmac-secret (one machine, one token)
setup.processes: one broadcaster and four member processes, loopback UDP; 30 s rounds on a virtual clock
setup.frames: not MACed (the per-epoch anonymous MAC key is not built)
setup.rust_replay: src/dcnet.rs a_recorded_cell_run_matches_the_rust_cell: CellPads from the recorded pads must give each broadcast body, and group_sum each decoded outcome
setup.host: owner's laptop on battery, 400 MHz (not a timing test)

runs.finding: 3 of 4 collision rounds decoded as an event nobody sent (kinds 1+3, 2+1, 3+0 senders' kinds XOR to a valid kind); the Rust replay agreed, so both implementations shared it

runs.run: after the fix (72-bit truncated SHA-256 tag)
after the audit's state fixes (locked, reloaded book state)

notes: The incident: docs/INCIDENTS.md, 'DC-net collisions could decode as an event nobody sent'.
Unit tests reproducing both failures on the old code: a_collision_of_two_kinds_never_decodes_as_an_event, a_member_cannot_turn_an_event_into_another_by_xor.
